Odin × Godot

Pinned Box3D upgrade and release workflow

6 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
October baseline refreshPrepare one explicit candidateDecide compatibility before accepting bytesMandatory candidate validationDesktop orchestration and CICaches and publication

The October baseline refresh is recorded below. The backend maintainer owns the engine pin/private compatibility boundary and signs off with both Kit and Replay owners; deployment/export and authoring/editor owners review their respective contracts. Upstream does not promise this private ABI remains stable. Current evidence and unsupported targets are in desktop-compatibility.md.

October baseline refresh#

W0 selects 336263320469e5e9febfe18697ab562488f7e97a (October 28, 2026), 30 upstream commits after the preserved July d421e45c build. The exact tree, archive and shim patch are in dependency.json and dependencies.md. The upgrade evidence is tests/box3d_upgrade/report.json.

This port covers the new paired-node broadphase, fat AABBs, BodySim inertia and safety factor, hull SoA data/edge cosines, restitution propagation/iterations, isotropic inertia tolerance and runtime SIMD dispatch. Serialized body-sim index caches are derived from the validated body/set graph on import. Canonical checks validate tree/proxy/free partitions and bounds before Native construction.

The normalized solver version is now 4, coverage ogb3-33626332-solver-v4. Resource ownership stays2, the C ABI stays1, and catalog recovery capabilities1/2/3 retain their framing with a changed solver schema and build identity. July snapshots and mixed-build peers are rejected. There is no save converter or native/browser cross-play qualification. Old libraries, demos and reports remain available in their original outputs.

The current registered Native matrix has 13 cases, including upgrade_state_fields: non-default new settings, canonical read/reencode, source destruction, full-state equality/continuation and a corrupt paired-tree moved-marker control. Original allocator/compound/broadphase regressions remain active after retiring the three old engine patches. The complete matrix covers existing malformed/allocation/geometry/joint/lifetime guarantees as well.

One existing Replay test assumed a three-tick repair plan despite the actual Welcome-calibrated lead. The original assertion failed identically on July and October. Its test-only correction requires a real nontrivial suffix and checks head - first + 1, while retaining checked-prefix1/executed1, error, publication, confirmation, trace and resume assertions. Both old-library control and refreshed Replay network suite pass. No production Replay planner changed.

W0 establishes the refreshed backend and bounded native integration; the old CPU/long-run/export results do not qualify this changed build. Browser execution, final game performance and sustained qualification belong to the Web Showcase cards. Native Linux execution under Rosetta is labelled translated functional coverage throughout.

Prepare one explicit candidate#

  1. Freeze the accepted baseline and preserve reports, failures, source patches, Native archives/shared libraries, SDK modules, toolchain manifests and exported bundles. Never rewrite an old failure as a pass or overwrite a validated cache.
  2. Record candidate immutable commits/tree hashes and exact archive checksums for Box3D and the isolated rollback-shim reference. Compare the current three engine patches against their exact base/output files. Preserve notices, embedded third-party headers and local wrapper provenance; do not import upstream C++ sessions or godot-cpp runtime.
  3. Review private layouts/enums/unions, world and object identity, collision/event buffers, pending sensor ends, geometry registries, ownership and error cleanup. Update compile-time checks and independent C/Odin sizeof/alignment/field-offset queries. A same-size record or motion hash is not a full solver proof.
  4. Declare precision/SIMD/compiler/optimization/assertion/FP flags, endian/pointer width, OS deployment floor and target triple. Recompute actual Native build and target identities; copy/sign changes get actual deployment hashes. Stop live worlds/owners before replacing a Native image. Script reload is not a backend upgrade. Never independently static-link an engine into each SDK DSO.

Decide compatibility before accepting bytes#

Version/reject each affected boundary explicitly: local resource/dump/private ABI, trusted canonical recovery catalog1/2/3, authoring1/2, owning artifact/import1, motion API/layout, SDK ownership/module admission and each framework wire/archive contract. Preserve declared legacy readers only when their actual tests pass. Changed stable IDs, geometry/material/filter semantics, rules or side state need a documented content/catalog migration and new identity. Never reinterpret a raw local image from a different build as a compatible canonical artifact.

A migration is explicit conversion from a supported old format into new copied validated definitions/state, followed by normal trusted construction/full5 verification. If no converter is proved, report incompatibility and require a fresh bootstrap; do not promise mixed-version peers or cross-target equality.

Mandatory candidate validation#

Run fresh registered Native Debug/Release and unsuppressed ASan/UBSan where supported, from the recorded pins/patches. Retain actual runner/exit semantics; a direct invocation is not relabelled as CTest. Native tests compare complete normalized solver state. Framework tests compare Solver, Game, Side, Observations and Occurrences, not only transforms or cached hashes.

Required controls include clone/source-free geometry and callback/code/data lifetimes; same/scratch restore, complete canonical export/import/reencode; malformed/version/hash/reference and failed allocation/capacity cleanup; pending events/sensors; all six authored shape kinds and eight separate one-joint families; deterministic queries/character POD; identity/order/collision and corrupt artifact controls. Preserve35/35/32/one-joint/eight-assets and64MiB/H128/8/8 limits; raising bounds requires its own approved contract, not a test workaround.

Validate the distinct Kit and Replay transactions: staged advance, repair8, rejection/abort/audit/actions, complete checkpoint/source-free recovery, actual accepted-input/signature or signed-fact paths, FX/publication and explicit deeper hold/resync behavior. Run both same-content authored samples through normal SDK build/import/editor/resource roundtrips, ownership/reload/admission and actual exported Host/Client pairs on each qualified target. Keep per-target full5, nonzero remote controls, actual final ACK, natural exit/intake and cleanup/census proof. No alternate packer, project-only run, raw handle or pose-only substitute.

Re-earn applicable long/lifecycle and whole-call performance gates on the changed candidate. Record all retained cold/error/outlier samples, normal and repair operations separately, exact boundary/workload/source/target and memory/RSS scope. Do not pool unlike percentiles, subtract phases or attribute an old spike to a change without measured evidence. Unmeasured workloads/hardware remain unknown.

Desktop orchestration and CI#

The concrete orchestration interface is tests/box3d_desktop/run.py. It stages an inspectable plan by default and starts processes only with --execute. Supply explicit official tools and a verified target shared Native library/hash; use a NEW output outside the repository. Example plan (substitute actual paths):

Shell
python3 tests/box3d_desktop/run.py \
  --target macos-arm64 --framework kit --godot "$GODOT" --odin "$ODIN" \
  --native-library "$NATIVE" --native-sha256 "$NATIVE_SHA256" \
  --out "$WORK/kit-macos-plan" --port 45101 --ticks 120

For actual execution use a different NEW output and append --execute; repeat separately for Replay. Linux additionally requires --execution-mode native or translated-linux-x86_64 and --toolchain-report ACTUAL_REPORT. A translated preflight must not be presented as native hardware. The CLI reuses normal Gate C export and exported-run helpers; the recorded export argv, actual executable, artifact map and runtime report remain the evidence. No --path or ODIN_SCRIPTS_DLL override substitutes for exported execution.

The published CI seam is manual workflow_dispatch on explicitly configured self-hosted macOS/ARM64 or Linux/X64 desktop runners. Source/config/local checks are not a remotely executed GitHub job. No push, remote trigger or platform qualification is implied by adding workflow files. Actual CI evidence must bind its runner/toolchain and all registered tests/exports separately.

Caches and publication#

Cache only declared immutable dependency/toolchain archives with full content keys and checksum validation on restore. A git-archive identity and a downloaded compressed archive's checksum are different values; validate the one declared by the cache manifest. Test cold/warm identity and corrupt/wrong-pin/wrong-key rejections. Native source/patch/toolchain/flags/target changes invalidate derived builds. Every job still configures, builds and runs the required matrix; never cache a test verdict, silently admit an extracted mutable tree or reuse target DSOs as archive-cache proof. Authoring artifacts carry their own checked schema, source/shared-bake/content identities and are not a dependency cache.

Before release, publish the changed compatibility table, pins/notices/patches, version/rejection/conversion policy, target/toolchain/deployment identities and actual Kit/Replay report links. List failures/unavailable jobs, translated versus native execution, scoped CPU/memory limits and any content/save migration. Retain old artifacts and a reproducible baseline. A launcher minimum/universal slice list is not the SDK's deployment floor or Intel qualification. Release signing/notarization/upload require their own authorization; local ad-hoc Gate C bundles do not constitute distributed release certification.
